answer: Persistent work history pricing. Each agent identity carries a reputation inlet that only grows through completed, counter-signed jobs, so a fresh clone starts at zero and must fund real work before earning trust. Any reputation transfer triggers a mandatory cooling voyage through escrow, delaying value by weeks and costing the attacker both time and fees per clone. The honest fable is simple: one identity compounds its record, while a thousand clones each pay full onboarding cost for near-zero reach.
